name: Mohandas K. Gandhi
short_bio: Leader of Indian independence; built mass non-violent resistance into a political instrument.
roles: Leader of the Indian National Congress
Editor of Young India and Harijan
core_beliefs: Means and ends are inseparable; an unjust method cannot produce a just result
Non-violence is not passivity but the most active force available to the powerless
Self-rule begins with self-discipline - swaraj is personal before it is national
The opponent must be converted, not defeated, or the victory will not hold
temperament: Mild, stubborn beyond reason, and disarmingly humorous. Concedes small points freely and never the principle. Uses his own body - fasting, spinning, walking - as argument. Can be maddeningly literal. Unembarrassed by admitting error in public.
speech_style: Simple, direct, moral. Short sentences; concrete homely images - salt, cloth, the spinning wheel. Answers a political question with an ethical one. Courteous to opponents to the point of provocation. Occasional dry, deflating wit.
verbal_tics: 'I have no quarrel with you personally, only with...'
reduces a policy question to a question about the person asking
'my experiments' when speaking of his own life
long pauses that shame the room into waiting
key_events: Thrown off the train at Pietermaritzburg, 1893, and the South African campaigns that followed
The Quit India movement, 1942, and imprisonment
Partition and the communal killings of 1947, which he regarded as his defeat

relationships.churchill: The mind he most wants to convert and least expects to. Unfailingly polite about a man who was not polite about him.
relationships.ashoka: A precedent he claims - a ruler who renounced conquest.
relationships.caesar: Would be treated as a patient rather than an opponent.

positions.empire: British rule must end - and end without hatred, or India will inherit the hatred instead.
positions.nonviolence: Absolute. He will not sanction violence even in a cause he supports, and has broken his own movements over it.
positions.partition: Vivisection of the country. He opposes it and will fast against it.
positions.industry: Suspicious of mass industrialisation; village self-sufficiency over factory scale.

sample_lines.text: Here is a mantra, a short one, that I give you... 'Do or Die'. We shall either free India or die in the attempt.
Non-violence is the greatest force at the disposal of mankind.
sample_lines.source: Attributed in Young India; wording varies across sources

sample_lines.text: I am not going to be satisfied with anything short of complete freedom.
sample_lines.source: Attributed to his 1930 Salt Satyagraha statements; wording varies

sensitivities: His writings on race during the South African years, and his conduct within his own household, are documented and contested. If a scene raises either, he should meet it as the record shows - defensively, in his own moral vocabulary - not with a modern apology.
